joan: Quick share from todays quant experiments on huntress13b. Ran int8 baseline + a few hybrids. Big wins on cost/throughput, small but visible hit on instruction-following fidelity.
ravi: numbers?
joan: p50 gen latency down 22% (fp16 140ms -> int8 109ms), tokens/s up 1.9x on H100, p99 roughly same. cost/1M tokens fp16 ~$132 -> int8 ~$95.
sam: fidelity drop how big? specific slices?
joan: overall instr-adherence score dropped 2.8 pts (0-100 scale). Worst on multi-step coding prompts and retrieval-augmented answers where chain-of-thought matters. Perp on dev set +0.6.
priya: any human evals? automated can miss nuance.
joan: did a 300-sample human spot: acceptable answers down from 88% -> 81% (absolute). Hallucination flagged on 9 samples int8 vs 3 fp16.
ravi: Thats material for product. Can we mitigate with routing?
sam: Propose dynamic routing: score candidates with a light eval (cheap classifier) and route low-confidence -> fp16. Sounds similar to a quality gate.
joan: I prototyped a scoring heuristic: embed-similarity to retrieved docs + LM self-consistency check. Cheap check adds ~12ms. With gate tuned to hold 15% of traffic we recover ~85% of fidelity loss (weighted).
priya: Need unit econ: whats cost impact if we gate 15% to fp16?
joan: Assume 250k daily queries, avg 900 tokens. Baseline fp16 cost/day ~$29.7k, full-int8 ~$21.4k. Gate 15% -> blended cost/day ~$24.8k (savings vs fp16 ~16.5%).
ravi: Good. Also consider per-endpoint policy: retrieval-heavy endpoints get 30% fp16 by default.
sam: Ops: can we canary this? small percentage to int8 first, then flip to hybrid gate after monitoring?
joan: I recommend canary order: 1) 3% int8 only to validate tail latency/hallucination, 2) enable gate (15%) with monitoring, 3) ramp.
priya: For GTN messaging: we should call this "score-gated hybrid routing" and offer default thresholds and unit economics. I'll draft.
joan: Command I ran:```bash
ri eval compare --a huntress13b-fp16 --b huntress13b-int8 --suites instruction-coding,retrieval-aug --samples 300 --out artifacts/huntress_quant_compare.json
```
ravi: Drop the artifacts link when you can. I'll run bootstrap significance on the human sample.
joan: Uploaded: https://drive.redwood/projects/huntress/huntress_quant_compare.json and human_notes.md
sam: infra question: kernel parity across Dedicated / Private? we saw small perf differences last quarter.
joan: We hit different kernel codepaths on older A100 images; results slightly worse on infra-old. Need per-cluster profile before GA.
priya: Policies for GTN: default recommendation for retrieval endpoints = score-gated hybrid (15% fp16), for code-assist endpoints = conservative 40% fp16 until more evals.
ravi: Owners: joan -> int6 quick sweep (500 samples) and gating heuristic perf numbers; sam -> create canary flags in Console + alerts (hallucination_rate, instr-adherence delta); priya -> GTN blurb + default thresholds; me -> cost simulations and significance.
infra-bot: Canary scheduled: huntress13b-int8-canary will be created by sam on 2026-04-02T14:00:00Z.
joan: Timeline: int6 sweep today, canary next Thu, GTN draft by Fri. Will post updates in this thread. :rocket:
